speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to determine the underlying cause, please describe your specific symptoms, when they started, and any associated neurological or systemic issues.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That describes significant ataxia; is the clumsiness constant or does it worsen with specific movements like finger-to-nose testing? Also, have you noticed any changes in your vision, speech, or balance when closing your eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy). Given your history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, and the new onset of gait and limb ataxia, this is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation. We need to confirm this immediately with an MRI of the brain to look for characteristic white matter lesions.
